# Model card: BreastCare AI mass-malignancy risk model

Structure after Mitchell et al. (2019), *Model Cards for Model Reporting*. All numbers are generated
from `models/model_metadata.json`; the full evaluation is in
[reports/evaluation.md](../reports/evaluation.md).

## Model details

| Model | Logistic regression (C=0.1) |
| Inputs | age, shape, margin, density (BI-RADS assessment excluded) |
| Output | P(malignant) (no calibration step applied), 90% conformal prediction set, class at threshold 0.514 |
| Trained on | fit split (n=498) of the UCI Mammographic Mass data |
| Calibration | `none` (chosen by CV Brier on out-of-fold predictions) |
| Conformal | Mondrian (class-conditional) split conformal, LAC score; Benign in set if p ≤ 0.577, Malignant if p ≥ 0.415 |
| Evaluation | held-out test set, n = 167, 95% bootstrap CIs |

**Main metrics (test set):** AUROC 0.90 (0.84–0.94) · Brier 0.132 (0.110–0.160) · sensitivity 0.90 (0.83–0.96) · specificity 0.81 (0.72–0.89) · conformal coverage 0.87 (0.81–0.92).

- Developed as a research and educational portfolio project (2026). Code and data provenance are in
  this repository.
- The served model is chosen by a fixed rule (lowest 5-fold CV log-loss on the fit split; a simpler
  model within one standard error is preferred). Candidates were logistic regression, LightGBM
  monotone in age and shape, and unconstrained LightGBM.

## Research comparison models

The served model above is the only model whose estimate is the assessment. Five further classifier
families exist for comparison: a random forest, histogram gradient boosting, a support vector machine
with an RBF kernel, k-nearest neighbours and a small neural network (one hidden layer). They are
trained by `python -m src.ml.zoo` and saved in `models/zoo/`, separately from the served model.

- **Same protocol as the served model.** Same cleaned data and the same stratified split (the split
  ids are checked against `models/splits.json`), the same four inputs (BI-RADS assessment excluded) and
  the same 5-fold cross-validation folds on the fit split. Each family has a small fixed grid; the grid
  point with the lowest mean cross-validated log-loss is kept. Calibration method and both thresholds
  come from out-of-fold predictions on the fit split, and the final model is trained on the whole fit
  split. Non-tree models use the logistic regression's preprocessing; tree models use the raw codes.
- **Reported, not used to choose.** The test split is used only to report each model's metrics, with
  the same bootstrap resamples as the served model, plus a paired AUROC difference against the served
  model. The results are in `models/zoo_metadata.json` (served at `/api/model-info` → `zoo`); one case
  can be run through every model at `POST /api/assess-models`. This card states no numbers for them.
- **The served model is unchanged.** It, its metadata and its selection rule (`src/ml/models.py`) do
  not depend on these models. They were added after the served model was chosen, so choosing one of
  them because of its test result would tune on the test split, and that test result would then
  overstate how well it generalises. The test split is also small, so the differences are mostly
  within the intervals. A different model could be considered only through a new, pre-specified
  selection rule evaluated on new data.
- These models have no conformal prediction sets and no explanations.

## Intended use

- **Primary use:** demonstrating how a clinical decision-support pipeline can be built and evaluated
  honestly: probabilities with measured calibration, conformal prediction sets, explanations, and documentation
  generated from the evaluation itself.
- **Primary users:** students, engineers and researchers studying trustworthy ML.
- **Out of scope:** diagnosis, screening or biopsy decisions for real patients; any use without a
  qualified clinician; inputs other than the four BI-RADS descriptors; populations unlike the training
  data (for example other countries, devices or time periods). It is not a medical device.

## Factors

- **Inputs are radiologist judgements.** Shape, margin and density are BI-RADS descriptors assigned by a
  reader, so the model inherits inter-reader variability.
- **Age.** Evaluated in two subgroups (below). Risk rises steeply with age, so the age term moves
  younger patients' estimates down.
- **Density.** About 90% of masses share one density value, so its effect is barely estimable.
- **Setting.** One German institute, full-field digital mammograms, 2003–2006.

## Metrics

AUROC and AUPRC (discrimination); Brier score, calibration slope and intercept, and ECE (calibration);
sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV at a threshold chosen on development data; empirical coverage of
the conformal sets, overall and per class; net benefit (decision curve). Every metric has a 95%
bootstrap interval on the held-out test set.

## Training and evaluation data

UCI Mammographic Mass (id 161, CC BY 4.0; [provenance](../data/README.md)). 961 raw cases, 831 after
dropping rows with missing values. Stratified split: 60% fit (training, cross-validation, calibration,
thresholds), 20% conformal calibration, 20% test (used once). The radiologists' BI-RADS assessment is
excluded from the inputs because it would leak the label; it is used only as a reference.

## Ethical considerations

- **False reassurance** is the main harm: a low estimate must never replace work-up of a suspicious
  mass. The decision curve in the evaluation report shows whether the model adds value at the low
  thresholds clinicians use for recommending biopsy (about 2%).
- **Over-reliance:** outputs are labelled as research estimates, carry a conformal set that says when
  the model cannot separate outcomes, and in the default chat mode every LLM answer passes input guardrails and a
  diagnostic-language filter. The assistant is evaluated separately (retrieval, faithfulness, red team) in
  [reports/rag_evaluation.md](../reports/rag_evaluation.md); its numbers do not describe the risk model.
- **Privacy:** the dataset is de-identified public research data; the app can store entered features in a
  local SQLite audit log when an API client starts an audit session; the web UI does not start one.

## Caveats and recommendations

- Small, single-site test set: confidence intervals are wide. Treat the cross-validated AUROC on the fit
  split as the more conservative estimate.
- Calibration should be re-checked before any use on new data. Check the slope reported above.
- Conformal coverage is guaranteed on average over random calibration and test draws, not for every split.
- Thresholds are illustrative. A real deployment would set them with clinicians, from the costs of
  missed cancers against unnecessary biopsies, and might use subgroup-aware thresholds.
- External validation on independent data is required before drawing any clinical conclusion.
